title: How do I get professors to answer my emails?
en:
*Give them the control for planning their day*

Scheduling a meeting:

Don't: When will you be available?
Do: I am available ... Will you be available in one of the time slots?

When you ask for availability, you are effectively asking for commitment for ALL of the time slots.

title: How do I get professors to answer my emails?
en:
*Calendar invite*

Once you scheduled a meeting. Please do send a calendar invite with all the required information (e.g., zoom link). 

Whatever that's not on their calendar does not exist.

title: How do I get professors to answer my emails?
en:
*Go 90% and let them finish the 10%*

• Need a form? Pre-fill it as much as you can (you know their name and email).
• Need a cover letter? Write a draft first.
• Need a ref. letter? Send an updated CV and SOP.
• Need to ask about a course? Read the syllabus first.

title: How do I get professors to answer my emails?
en:
*cc all parties involved*

Asking for some code/data/clarification? cc'ing your PI and their PI definitely helps you get a prompt reply!

title: How do I get professors to answer my emails?
en:
*Don't cc all parties involved*

Don't send requests to MULTIPLE people in the same thread. Everyone will assume others will do it and therefore no one will do it. Send INDIVIDUAL emails instead.

title: How do I get professors to answer my emails?
en:
*One email one topic*

Help your professors respond your email quickly. Make your emails simple, clear, and actionable.

title: How do I get professors to answer my emails?
en:
*Formatting*

You are not writing in plain texts. 
Formatting your email so that it's easy to read, e.g., 
• bullet points for parallel concepts
• bold font for highlighting 
• bold phrase for organizing your email
• italic for sentence stress

title: How do I get professors to answer my emails?
en:
*Timeline*

Provide specific action and specific date that the task needed to be completed. This helps them plan their schedule to make time for your requests.
How to save for retirement as a graduate student (in the US)?

title: How to save for retirement as a graduate student (in the US)?
en: How to save for retirement as a graduate student (in the US)?

title: How to save for retirement as a graduate student (in the US)?
en:
*Why?*

"Don't make fun of graduate students. They just made a terrible life choice." - The Simpsons

Yes, grad students are paid poorly. But with income from RA/TA/fellowships/internships, there usually are leftover money. 

❌ Do nothing
✅ Invest in *tax-advantaged* accounts

title: How to save for retirement as a graduate student (in the US)?
en:
*Why save early?*

When you save and invest for retirement early, you get to enjoy the power of compounding for your investments.

Ideally, max out the contribution limit (6K a year).

title: How to save for retirement as a graduate student (in the US)?
en:
*How to save?*

Two types of Individual Retirement Accounts (IRAs):

👉 Traditional: Save now, tax later
👉 Roth: Tax now, save later

As grad students are in the low-tax bracket, Roth IRA would probably make more sense. 

Earnings growth + withdrawals in retirement: *tax free*

title: How to save for retirement as a graduate student (in the US)?
en:
*Why now?*

Previously, graduate students who are on fellowship stipends or grants would have difficulty in funding their IRAs because those income are not considered "taxable compensation".

But that change in Dec 2019, making it easy for all grad students to save!

title: How to save for retirement as a graduate student (in the US)?
en:
*What if I really need the money after graduation?*

✅ Withdraw Roth IRA contributions (not earnings) are tax free and penalty free.

✅ Several early withdrawals of earnings can still be tax/penalty free, e.g., 1st home purchase, large medical expenses, education.

title: How to save for retirement as a graduate student (in the US)?
en:
Happy Saving! 

Disclaimer: Clearly this is NOT a financial advice. You should definitely check out more information and make your own decisions. 

But, I wish I knew about all these options and tax-benefits when I was a grad student (especially for international students).

title: How to save for retirement as a graduate student (in the US)?
en:
@kushalchawla18 Investment via brokerage account:
- Various sources of income like interest, dividends, capital gains (when you sell an investment for a profit) are all subject to taxes. 

Investment via Roth IRA:
- Earnings growth and qualified withdraws are tax-free.

title: How to save for retirement as a graduate student (in the US)?
en:
@whyisyoung You can still contribute to the 2021 Roth IRA before April 18 2022.

You are right about the income restriction. For that you can explore either back door IRA (before it is banned) or rollover from other retirement accounts such as 401k later.
